phase: base lab environment; OIDC fixture with two issuers running

steps.action: Configure single sign-on step 3: the Identity providers card, Add provider, and its fields; Register provider with an issuer that cannot be reached is refused
steps.expected: Dialog with Display name, Provider ID, Issuer URL, Email domains, Client ID, Client secret; the comma help; refused; nothing registered
steps.actual: Add provider opened a dialog with the labels ["Display name","Provider ID","Issuer URL","Email domains","Client ID","Client secret"]. The Email domains help read "Separate several domains with commas. Sign-in routes by the email domain a person enters, so each domain can belong to one provider.". Register provider with an unreachable issuer showed "The server could not be reached. Try again." in the dialog and no provider was stored.

steps.action: Configure single sign-on steps 1, 3 and 4: the operator's OIDC client (local fixture); Register provider; copy the displayed callback URL; registration turns on nothing; the secret is never returned
steps.expected: Row with display name, domain and Configured; callback ends /api/auth/sso/callback on the instance address; SSO switches stay off but become available
steps.actual: Register provider closed the dialog. The card listed ["DOC-032 Helix IdP helix.example Configured Saved"]. Below the card: "Sign-in routes by the email domain a person enters, so each domain belongs to one provider. Removing a provider deletes its configuration; accounts keep their rows. Paste this callback URL into your IdP console: http://127.0.0.1:43351/api/auth/sso/callback". The instance address is BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:43351. Both group policies were unchanged and both Single sign-on (SSO) switches were off and available (["false","false"]). GET /api/v1/auth/sso-providers did not contain the client secret.

steps.action: Configure single sign-on steps 5 and 6: turn on SSO under Legal User Authentication; with one provider the sign-in page offers a single Continue with single sign-on button; an invited staff account signs in through the identity provider
steps.expected: Single button, no email field; callback succeeds; role Legal team member; the invited row becomes Active
steps.actual: The switch showed "Saved". In a separate browser the staff sign-in page offered one Continue with single sign-on button and no Email field (by email: false). It went through http://oidc:8080/authorize and the OpenLaw callback to /, signed in as legal_team_member. The invited row now read Active with a role control (true).

steps.action: Matching an allowed email domain does not grant an uninvited person a staff role
steps.expected: No staff session and no staff account
steps.actual: With Business Portal SSO off and helix.example on the allowed list, doc032-auth-uninvited-p11119@helix.example ended on /auth/login?error=sso with me 401 and "Single sign-on failed. Try again.". Account created: none.

steps.action: Update a registered provider: Edit {name}; Provider ID is fixed; Save provider with Client secret blank keeps it; a replacement rotates it; test a fresh sign-in after each
steps.expected: No Provider ID field; the Client secret help; saved both times; SSO works after each
steps.actual: Edit DOC-032 Helix IdP opened a dialog with no Provider ID field and an empty Client secret; its help read "Leave blank to keep the current secret. Paste a new value to rotate.". Saving a Client ID change with the secret blank closed the dialog; a fresh staff SSO sign-in worked (me 200). Saving a replacement secret closed the dialog; another fresh sign-in worked (me 200).

steps.action: Update negative: an issuer that cannot be reached is refused and the previous provider configuration stays in place
steps.expected: Refused; stored issuer unchanged; SSO still works
steps.actual: Save provider with an unreachable issuer showed "The server could not be reached. Try again." in the dialog. The stored issuer stayed http://oidc:8080 and a fresh staff SSO sign-in still worked (me 200).

steps.action: Several identity providers: register a second provider with two comma-separated domains; every provider uses the same callback URL
steps.expected: Two rows; the second lists both domains and Configured; the callback is the same
steps.actual: Register provider closed the dialog; the callback shown was http://127.0.0.1:43351/api/auth/sso/callback, the same as for the first provider. Rows: ["DOC-032 Helix IdP helix.example Configured","DOC-032 Harbor IdP harbor.example, ops.northwind.example Configured Saved"]. Stored domains ["harbor.example","ops.northwind.example"].

steps.action: An email domain can belong to one provider only: an exact domain, a subdomain, and a parent domain of another provider's domain are refused, naming the provider that holds it
steps.expected: Three refusals, each naming the holder; nothing stored
steps.actual: Refusals: {"exact":{"outcome":"alert","alert":"helix.example is already assigned to the identity provider DOC-032 Helix IdP. Each email domain can belong to one provider."},"subdomain":{"outcome":"alert","alert":"eu.harbor.example overlaps harbor.example, which is assigned to the identity provider DOC-032 Harbor IdP. Each email domain can belong to one provider."},"parent":{"outcome":"alert","alert":"northwind.example overlaps ops.northwind.example, which is assigned to the identity provider DOC-032 Harbor IdP. Each email domain can belong to one provider."}}. The provider list still held 2 providers.

steps.action: With two or more providers, the sign-in page asks for the email address and opens the provider that serves its domain; an unserved domain shows the no-provider message and other methods stay available
steps.expected: Email form with its hint; helix.example goes to the first issuer, harbor.example to the second; the unserved-domain message
steps.actual: The staff sign-in page read "Enter your work email. Your organization's identity provider opens next." with an Email field. An unlisted.example address showed "No single sign-on provider is set up for unlisted.example. Check the address or contact your administrator.", and the page still offered ["Continue with single sign-on","Email me a sign-in link","Sign in with a password"]. doc032-auth-sso-p11119@helix.example was routed to http://oidc:8080 and signed in (legal_team_member). The invited doc032-auth-harbor-p11119@harbor.example was routed to http://oidc:8082 and signed in as legal_team_member; the row read Active.

steps.action: Missing credentials: a provider whose stored configuration lost its client ID shows Missing credentials; editing it and entering the client ID and secret again shows Configured
steps.expected: Missing credentials chip after the fault; Configured after Save provider
steps.actual: After blanking the stored configuration of doc032-harbor in the database, the row read "DOC-032 Harbor IdP harbor.example, ops.northwind.example Missing credentials". Edit, Client ID and Client secret entered again, and Save provider closed the dialog; the row read "DOC-032 Harbor IdP harbor.example, ops.northwind.example Configured" and a Harbor staff sign-in worked again (me 200).

steps.action: Turn on SSO under Business Portal Authentication: an existing Business User signs in through the identity provider, and still can after its domain is removed; a new identity on the removed domain is refused
steps.expected: Portal before and after narrowing; newcomer refused with no account
steps.actual: doc032-auth-ssobu-p11119@helix.example entered the Portal through a sign-in link. The Business Portal SSO switch showed "Saved". Portal single sign-on (email form: true) reached /portal/onboarding as business_user. After Remove helix.example (list ["northwind.example"], not empty), the same identity still signed in through single sign-on (/portal/onboarding, business_user). A new identity on the removed domain ended on /portal/login?error=sso with "Single sign-on failed. Try again." and no account was created. helix.example was added back (Business SSO true).

steps.action: Recover from a failing provider: with only SSO on under Legal, Administrator password sign-in still works; turn on Email and password and turn off SSO
steps.expected: Administrator sign-in link; admin password sign-in works; Legal Team Member password sign-in works again; SSO off
steps.actual: With only Single sign-on (SSO) on for Legal users ({"password":false,"magicLink":false,"sso":true,"requireTwoFactor":false}), the staff page offered ["Continue with single sign-on","Administrator sign-in"] and Daniel still signed in with a password through Administrator sign-in (me 200). Turning Email and password and Email magic link back on and SSO off in both cards gave {"legal":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false},"business":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}}, and Nadia signed in with a password again (me 200).
